messages:
maria.support: Customer (AcmeRetail) escalated — streaming JSON mode returns a truncated object mid-key on ~10% of requests. They say it happens when using our SSE endpoint through their proxy. They attached a curl repro and a sample truncated payload.

maria.support: Repro curl from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -v -N \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" \\
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses?mode=json&model=redwood-large\"
```

maria.support: Truncated payload snippet they saw: `{"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"...\n  \"summary\": \"Completed analysis of Q1 ...` (stops mid-string, no closing braces).

alex.eng: Thanks — tagging @sam.sre. First-pass: sounds like early FIN or proxy flush. Do we have edge logs for that request_id?

sam.sre: I pulled logs for their request-id (r-4299xxxx). Saw connection close from 10.1.4.22 (their proxy) after a 2s idle gap. Edge shows keepalive heartbeats from our service, then FIN from upstream.

sam.sre: Hypothesis: proxy (or client) has 2s idle timeout and treats SSE as idle between big chunks, closes connection mid-chunk. That will produce a truncated JSON object.

alex.eng: Does JSON-mode stream each object as single chunk? We stream SSE frames with chunked transfer encoding, objects can be sent in multiple TCP segments. If the proxy splits on packet boundaries and has an idle cutoff, we can lose tail.

maria.support: Customer says behavior increased after they enabled a caching gateway (nginx in front of their app). They repro by running curl from their network and sometimes get full JSON, sometimes partial.

alex.eng: Can we reproduce locally by putting nginx with low proxy_read_timeout between client and our SSE endpoint? If yes, that's a good reproduction path.

sam.sre: Quick repro steps I used: start a local nginx reverse-proxy with proxy_buffering on, proxy_read_timeout 2s, then curl through it. Repro rate ~30%.

sam.sre: Minimal nginx conf I used:
```
server {
  listen 8080;
  location /proxy/ {
    proxy_pass https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses?mode=json&model=redwood-large;
    proxy_buffering on;
    proxy_read_timeout 2s;
  }
}
```

alex.eng: Nice, that matches. Immediate mitigations for customer: 1) disable buffering/proxy_read_timeout tightenings on their gateway, 2) enable application-level heartbeats from our side (send a small SSE comment/heartbeat between objects) so proxies don't hit idle timeouts.

maria.support: Customer asked if we can change something server-side now. Can we add heartbeat comments in JSON-mode streaming without breaking structured parsing?

alex.eng: Yes — we can emit SSE comments like `: hb\n\n` between events, SSE comments are ignored by clients. But note some client parsers expecting pure JSON chunks may get confused if they don't skip comments. We should confirm our SDKs tolerate it.

sam.sre: Short-term patch: add header `X-Stream-Heartbeat: 1` toggles server to emit a 15s comment heartbeat. I'll open a patch and a canary rollout for hosted API routes.

alex.eng: Also add guidance to docs: when putting our streaming endpoint behind proxies, ensure proxy honors streaming/chunked responses (disable buffering) and increase read timeout. Add the nginx snippet.

maria.support: I told the customer those mitigations. They're going to test disabling the new caching gateway first. I'll update here after they try.

ingest-bot: Created ticket INF-8123 and assigned to eng-runtime. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8123

maria.support: Thanks — escalating to eng-runtime for the heartbeat toggle and docs update. I'll keep this thread for updates. :thumbsup:
